findings.title: All-groups VIEW satisfies canManage()
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, so a caller who only has the all-groups view scope is treated as allowed to manage groups. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (and any other requireManage() gate) therefore lets a view-only admin create groups. canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks only MANAGE, so the no-arg method is inconsistent with the per-group check and with V1, which required MANAGE_USERS. A view permission must not authorize mutations.

findings.title: View-members group filter uses authz resource ids
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() walks resources with findByType(GROUPS) and, on a match, calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the set later passed to user search/count as UserModel.GROUPS. FGAP group resources are stored by name equal to the group id (resolveGroup returns group.getId()), while getId() is the authorization resource primary key. The permission lookup therefore searches by the wrong name, misses the group policy, and falls back to the all-groups resource; the ids handed to getUsersCount/searchForUserStream are not group ids. Admins who only have view-members or manage-members on specific groups get an empty or wrong membership filter, so user search and counts omit those members (pagination is applied in the DB before the canView post-filter). The type resource named "Groups" is also included by findByType and must be skipped. Use the resource name (the group id) and evaluate that resource directly.

findings.title: Per-group FGAP resources are created without type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource creates a resource named with the group id and sets scopes, but never calls setType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). The all-groups resource created in init() does set type. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission relies on resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE), so individually permissioned groups are invisible to that scan even after the id/name bug is fixed. Set the type when creating the resource (same as the type-level resource).

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never get Groups schema
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and this PR adds the Groups resource type plus manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members scopes only on that first-time path. Realms that already enabled admin permissions V2 keep a client whose resource server has neither the Groups type resource nor the new scopes. Creating a group permission then fails in getOrCreateResource (ModelException "No scopes found") or scope validation, so the feature does not work on upgrade. init (or a migration) must add missing schema scopes and the Groups type resource to an existing admin-permissions client.

findings.title: Group removal calls V2-unsupported permission teardown
findings.body: registerListener still handles GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent by calling management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. This PR makes management() return MgmtPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. If both features are on, deleting a group fails the admin event listener and can abort the removal. The listener must no-op (or use a V2 cleanup) when the V2 evaluator is active.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
findings.body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false. The implementation throws when canManageMembers is false. Callers reading the contract will enforce the wrong scope (manage-membership vs manage-members).
